limits: Local macOS arm64 dry-run only; no hosted GitHub release API, SLSA provenance, or cross-platform binary was exercised.
The real rollback (yanking/replacing published assets, provenance re-attestation, release-notes edit) remains a human gate; see docs/release/runbook.md section 8.
Synthetic archives prove the checksum/replacement mechanics, not binary correctness.
mechanism_under_test: .github/workflows/release.yml release job 'Generate SHA-256 checksums file' step (sha256sum over *.tar.gz *.zip *.cdx.json, sorted) and asset-replacement semantics of softprops/action-gh-release (same-name upload replaces; SHA256SUMS must be regenerated in the same act).
scope: Offline dry-run of release.yml release-job checksum generation and asset replacement/rollback mechanics in /tmp; synthetic REHEARSAL stand-in archives, never real release binaries; no GitHub release, tag, or asset was created or touched.
steps: Created /tmp/forge-f22-rollback-rehearsal-v1 with staging/, artifacts/, quarantine/, restored/.
Placed four synthetic platform archives plus the committed draft SBOM as the .cdx.json stand-in.
Ran the exact release-job checksum snippet; sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS verified all five assets.

Simulated defect discovery: quarantined the linux archive, restored a prior-good stand-in, regenerated SHA256SUMS with the same snippet; verification passed and only the replaced asset's digest changed.
Negative control: appended bytes to one archive; sha256sum -c reported FAILED for exactly that asset (tamper detected).
